incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager duty: Incident triggered - service: cache-redis - symptom: connection_exhaustion - severity: P1 - Pager: eng-oncall. Root cause unknown. Please ack.

pagerduty: Incident 98765: cache-redis maxclients reached (auto-escalation in 7m) -- https://pd.example/org/incidents/98765

alice.dev: acked. I'm on it. seeing a huge spike in `connected_clients` on prod-redis-1 (5m avg ~ 10k, config maxclients=10000). lots of ephemeral connections from batch-worker pool.

caroline.sre: @alice.dev thanks. any 5xxs or timeouts reported? customer-alerts show increased 503s on /search and /chat endpoints.

alice.dev: yes, frontend 503s spiking. Error logs: `redis connection refused` and `ERR max number of clients reached`. 95th latency for cache reads up to 1.2s.

dave.oncall: rolling with me? I'm winding down another ticket but can pair. quick question: did we just deploy the ML scoring change ~ 10:10? could be new client behavior.

ml-platform: there was a micro-deploy at 10:05 that increased parallel scoring workers (env VAR SCORER_PAR=16 -> 32). I'm checking rollout history.

alice.dev: looks correlated. the batch job workers also restarted ~10:07 per kubernetes events. likely combined pressure.

caroline.sre: mitigation options: 1) increase redis `maxclients` temporarily on standby nodes (risk: memory), 2) throttle incoming connections via service mesh, 3) scale redis replicas / add proxied connection pool (twemproxy/hiredis proxy), 4) revert ML deploy. Which do we want first?

dave.oncall: can we throttle at ingress for the scorer route? simpler and low risk. If we reduce concurrency to 8 per pod that should cut connection churn.

alice.dev: I can patch the scorer HPA/Deployment to set `SCORER_PAR=8` and push a quick rollout. doing a canary on two pods first.

alice.dev: deploying patch now: `kubectl set env deploy/scorer SCORER_PAR=8 -n prod`

ops-bot: deploy started by alice.dev — deploy/scorer rollout: 1/6 -> 2/6 -> canary applied

alice.dev: canary pods are up. monitoring redis connected_clients...

caroline.sre: I'm adding a temporary iptables throttle on the batch job namespace to cap outgoing traffic to redis to avoid new flurries. Will revert after stable.

pagerduty: Acknowledgement received from alice.dev at 1951234580. Escalation timer paused.

alice.dev: connected_clients dropping from 10k -> 6.2k within 90s. errors on frontend down to baseline. 95th latency back to ~220ms. looks promising.

dave.oncall: nice. can we also patch redis config to increase `maxclients` to 15000 on replicas? Need a safer buffer if traffic bounces. Caroline, you okay with rolling config change?

caroline.sre: I'd prefer gradual: increase to 12000 first, monitor memory. will schedule a 2m rolling restart for redis-replica-1..3. doing `redis-cli CONFIG SET maxclients 12000` on leader and replicas to avoid immediate restarts.

alice.dev: note: a few client pools still leak when workers crash fast. short term we should enable `client-timeout` in pool lib to reclaim sockets earlier. adding a ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/OPS-4321

dave.oncall: good call. Also, can someone confirm if any VIP customers are affected?

alice.dev: support: some enterprise customers reported degraded search; no data loss. SLAs impacted for ~8 minutes for some queries. sending heads-up to account team.

sre-rotation: hey all — I'm taking the incident for the next 30m. handing off to @dave.oncall after I finish the redis config changes.

caroline.sre: redis config change applied to replicas via `CONFIG SET maxclients 12000`. memory usage per node up ~6% but within threshold. no swap. continuing to monitor.

ops-bot: metric alert suppressed: redis.connected_clients > 9000 (suppression window 10m) — incident in recovery.

pagerduty: Incident 98765 status: acknowledged -> resolved_by_policy candidate (no further alerts in 10m). Please confirm manual resolution.

dave.oncall: I'm closing the active page in 10m if metrics stable. next steps: 1) revert scorer concurrency to safe default with code fix to pool timeouts, 2) implement connection pooling at service layer (short-term proxy), 3) postmortem doc + customer impact summary.

alice.dev: agreed. creating a quick follow-up patch for pool timeouts and adding a regression test.

caroline.sre: adding action item: audit all deploys that change concurrency envs to have pre-deploy chaos checks.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident 98765 closed at 1951234599 by dave.oncall. Duration: 2 minutes. Follow-up Jira: OPS-4322. Postmortem meeting scheduled: today 16:00 PT.

dave.oncall: thanks everyone. filing brief customer status update. will attach timing and affected endpoints to the postmortem. :thumbsup:
